storyboard.claim: Who really invents our world? The pioneers, not chance.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host speaking to camera; no icon, the question itself is the picture.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Cold open of the episode.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: the callout restates the question rather than adding a fact.
storyboard.staging: Host speaks directly to camera, asking who really invents our world.

storyboard.claim: These people rewrite science, redefine art and overhaul culture.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host gesturing outward with both hands, open and wide.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Expands the pioneers into three fields.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the scope: science, art and culture, not one field.
storyboard.staging: Host gestures broadly, as if sweeping across fields of work.

storyboard.claim: The same people are fiercely disciplined and wildly playful at once.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host pausing mid-thought, weighing the two traits.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The pioneers now have a paradox attached.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the two opposite traits side by side in the callout.
storyboard.staging: Host pauses thoughtfully, holding the contradiction in mind.

storyboard.claim: The paradox is real but it is not random.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host thinking, tapping chin, considering the contradiction.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the paradox with the claim that it has a cause.
storyboard.addedInformation: Says the tension is systematic, not chance.
storyboard.staging: Host considers the contradiction and frames it as deliberate.

storyboard.claim: The tension between discipline and play drives discovery.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host talking with a firm gesture, emphasising the point.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the paradox into the mechanism.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names discovery as the output of the tension.
storyboard.staging: Host makes a firm gesture, presenting the tension as the driving mechanism.

storyboard.claim: Discipline alone only repeats what already exists.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host talking; the callout carries the claim, no icon fits a repetition cleanly.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: First half of the paradox: discipline on its own.
storyboard.addedInformation: Says discipline alone produces repetition, not new work.
storyboard.staging: Host talks in a steady, rational tone, describing repetition.

storyboard.claim: Discipline alone repeats; playfulness alone makes a mess; only both push forward.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A three-bucket sorter: discipline alone, playfulness alone, both together.
storyboard.onScreenText: DISCIPLINE ALONE / PLAYFULNESS ALONE / BOTH TOGETHER
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the two halves of the paradox into a comparison.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sorts the three outcomes the narrator describes into buckets.
storyboard.staging: Host presents the three buckets, a diagram beside the talking presenter.

storyboard.claim: Humanity moves forward only when both traits are present.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A road icon: the path forward that needs both traits.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Closes the paradox section and points to the episode topic.
storyboard.addedInformation: Links the paradox to progress for humanity.
storyboard.staging: Host gestures along the road icon, moving forward.

storyboard.claim: The episode is built on one arguable thesis.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host talking, no icon; the callout labels the thesis.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the paradox to the episode's central argument.
storyboard.addedInformation: Signals that the thesis is debatable, not settled.
storyboard.staging: Host introduces the thesis with a neutral, measured tone.

storyboard.claim: Creativity is not a magical gift that a few are born with.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host talking; the struck-through phrase carries the rejection, no gift icon (it would show a present, the opposite of the claim).
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The thesis rejects the gift myth.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strike makes the rejection visible without sound.
storyboard.staging: Host rejects the idea of a gift, the phrase crossed out.

storyboard.claim: Creativity is a system, not a trait.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host talking, no icon; the callout states the replacement idea.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Replaces the rejected gift with a system.
storyboard.addedInformation: weak: restates the thesis in plain words.
storyboard.staging: Host states the replacement claim plainly.

storyboard.claim: Three gears must interlock: person, field of gatekeepers, domain.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Three buckets: person, field, domain, the three gears of the system.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Breaks the system into its three parts.
storyboard.addedInformation: Lists the three parts the narrator names.
storyboard.staging: Host presents the three parts of the system as buckets.

storyboard.claim: Does seeing yourself as one cog make creativity less or more mysterious?
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host thinking, the question held in mind.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sets up the debate the episode will argue.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the debate as a choice between two outcomes.
storyboard.staging: Host considers the question, weighing both sides.

storyboard.claim: The premise comes from a decades-long study by Mihaly Csikszentmihalyi.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host in a library setting, the study's source.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the debate to its evidence.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the author and the study's length.
storyboard.staging: Host speaks in a quiet library, citing the study.

storyboard.claim: The study covers 91 exceptional people.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host in the library, the number carried by the callout.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Adds the sample size to the study.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the number of people studied.
storyboard.staging: Host talks steadily about the sample of 91.

storyboard.claim: The subjects include Nobel laureates, artists and business titans.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A trophy icon: prize and status, matching Nobel laureates.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Describes who the 91 people are.
storyboard.addedInformation: Lists the kinds of achievers in the sample.
storyboard.staging: Host gestures to the trophy, the status of the subjects.

storyboard.claim: The study looked at the invisible structure around the creators, not only their work.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host pointing at the empty space around him, the unseen structure.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from who was studied to what was studied.
storyboard.addedInformation: Says the focus was the surrounding structure.
storyboard.staging: Host points at the space around the work, not at the work.

callout.text: THE ORIGIN OF A NEW IDEA

storyboard.claim: Where does a truly new idea come from?
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host thinking; the callout asks the question.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns to the everyday stakes of creativity.
storyboard.addedInformation: Poses the central question of the episode.
storyboard.staging: Host considers the question with a thoughtful pause.

storyboard.claim: The lone genius staring out a window is a myth.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host talking; the struck-through phrase rejects the myth, no lightbulb (it would stage the rejected halo-of-light picture).
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Dismisses the romantic picture from the last beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strike marks the myth as rejected.
storyboard.staging: Host rejects the lone genius picture, the phrase crossed out.

callout.text: THE FIRST GEAR IS THE DOMAIN

storyboard.claim: The first gear of the system is the domain.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host talking, the callout names the first gear.
storyboard.onScreenText: THE FIRST GEAR IS THE DOMAIN
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Starts the walk through the three gears with the domain.
storyboard.addedInformation: Identifies the domain as the first of the three gears.
storyboard.staging: Host introduces the first gear with a firm gesture.

storyboard.claim: A domain is the set of rules, procedures and knowledge that already exists.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A game icon: a domain is a rule set to be learned, like a game.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Defines the domain just named.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the definition: rules, procedures, knowledge.
storyboard.staging: Host talks, a game icon beside him for the rule set.

storyboard.claim: You cannot change a domain until you learn its rules.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host holding a book: the rules to learn before changing anything.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sets up the golden rule of the domain.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the golden rule as learning before changing.
storyboard.staging: Host holds a book, the rules to be learned first.

callout.text: EUROPE AT THE END OF WAR

storyboard.claim: Europe at the end of World War II is the example.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A war icon: the war that ravaged the continent.
storyboard.onScreenText: EUROPE AT THE END OF WAR
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from the rule to a concrete example.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets the historical example in post-war Europe.
storyboard.staging: Host introduces the war-ravaged setting with the war icon.

storyboard.claim: The continent is half destroyed, rubble and broken bridges.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host with a worried look against a street setting; the callout carries the ruin.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Describes the setting of the example.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the physical ruin: rubble and bridges.
storyboard.staging: Host looks concerned while describing the ruined landscape.

storyboard.claim: The example is a 17-year-old named Manfred Eigen.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A young man standing in the ruined street; the callout names him.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the person into the ruined setting.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives his name and age, corrected from the ASR spelling.
storyboard.staging: A teenage figure stands in the street, introduced by name and age.

callout.text: ESCAPED A PRISONER OF WAR CAMP

storyboard.claim: He has escaped a prisoner of war camp and walks alone across the ruins.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The young man walking across the street, alone.
storyboard.onScreenText: ESCAPED A PRISONER OF WAR CAMP
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Follows the introduction with his escape.
storyboard.addedInformation: Says where he escaped from.
storyboard.staging: The young man walks forward, looking worried, through the ruins.

storyboard.claim: He walks straight to the city of Göttingen, not to safety or food.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A road icon: the direct path he takes to the city.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Says where he walks and why it is not safety.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the destination city and that it is a single goal.
storyboard.staging: The young man walks along the road, purposeful.

storyboard.claim: He has a strong hunger to be near the physics faculty as it rebuilds.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The young man in a bare classroom, thinking, the faculty not drawn.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the walk to his motive.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the hunger as a hunger for physics.
storyboard.staging: The young man thinks about the physics he wants to reach.

storyboard.claim: His only thought is to return to the science.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The young man in the classroom, troubled, thinking about the science.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: States his single goal.
storyboard.addedInformation: Says his one thought is returning to the science.
storyboard.staging: The young man thinks, intent on returning to the science.

storyboard.claim: He later wins a Nobel Prize in chemistry.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A trophy icon: the Nobel prize he eventually wins.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Pays off the journey with the outcome.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the prize and field.
storyboard.staging: The young man celebrates beside the trophy: a genuine win.

storyboard.claim: Mastering a domain costs a large amount of attention, our scarcest resource.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host talking, no icon; the callout names attention as the cost.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Generalises the example into the cost of learning.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names attention as the price paid.
storyboard.staging: Host explains the cost with a steady gesture.

storyboard.claim: Today the attention economy is mostly about phones taking attention.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A phone icon: the modern smartphone that takes attention.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Connects attention to modern life.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names phones as the modern attention thief.
storyboard.staging: Host refers to the phone icon as the modern distraction.

storyboard.claim: Creativity needs a large stockpile of surplus attention.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host talking; the callout carries the term surplus.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the author's term surplus.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the term surplus attention.
storyboard.staging: Host introduces the term with a steady tone.

callout.text: ATTENTION IS SPREAD ACROSS MANY HOBBIES

storyboard.claim: Surviving the day or scattering attention over many hobbies blocks breakthroughs.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host slumped with a worried look, exhausted by scattered attention.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains what drains surplus attention.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the two drains: survival and too many hobbies.
storyboard.staging: Host slumps, worn out by scattered attention.

storyboard.claim: Human attention is finite and the brain processes only a few bits per second.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host talking, the callout states the limit.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why surplus is scarce.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the limit: finite attention, few bits per second.
storyboard.staging: Host states the limit plainly.

storyboard.claim: People cannot learn physics, violin and cooking at once.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host talking, the callout denies superhuman multitasking.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the human limit a concrete form.
storyboard.addedInformation: Says humans are not built for multitasking at this scale.
storyboard.staging: Host speaks, reasoning about human limits.

storyboard.claim: Creativity needs surplus attention focused on one specific domain.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host thinking, the callout names the single focus.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Concludes the attention argument.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the single focus as the requirement.
storyboard.staging: Host considers the single focus needed.

storyboard.claim: Jacob Rabinow was a prolific inventor.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A middle-aged inventor at a workstation; the callout names him, corrected from the ASR spelling.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Moves from the principle to a named example.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the inventor.
storyboard.staging: The inventor talks at his workstation, introduced by name.

storyboard.claim: Rabinow over 200 US patents did not credit magic or muses.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The inventor talking at the workstation; the struck phrase rejects magic and muses (no lightbulb, which would read as inspiration).
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Describes how Rabinow explained his own mind.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strike marks magic and muses as rejected explanations.
storyboard.staging: The inventor dismisses magic, the phrase crossed out.

storyboard.claim: He described his brain as a specialised database built from decades of focused attention.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The inventor holding notes at the workstation, the knowledge store.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the mechanism behind his surplus.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the metaphor he used for his mind.
storyboard.staging: The inventor holds notes, the knowledge he built over decades.
